rejected.title: Self-determination
card: Self-determination is the right of a people to decide for themselves how they are governed and how they pursue their social, cultural and economic life.
For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, it means having a real say in decisions about their own lives, lands and communities. It is not only being asked for an opinion.

It can take many forms, such as Indigenous-run community organisations that deliver services like health care and legal help, and Indigenous people making the decisions about programs that affect them.
It contrasts with policies made for Indigenous peoples by governments, with little or no say from the people affected.
rejected.remember: Self-determination means Indigenous peoples making the decisions that affect them, not having decisions made for them.

a.q: Which situation best shows self-determination for an Aboriginal community?
opts: The community controls how its own health service is run
A government department designs a program, then tells locals
A government agency asks for comments, then decides alone
A council runs a cultural program with no community input
a.why: Self-determination means the community itself makes the decisions. Running its own health service does this. Being asked for comments is tempting, but the government still decides, so the community has no real say.
a.clue: Who holds the power to decide?

b.q: A state government plans a youth program for a remote Aboriginal community. It holds one meeting, listens to views, then writes the program itself. Why does this fall short of self-determination?
opts: The community did not make the decisions about the program
The government spent money on a community program
The community was told about the program before it began
The meeting was held in the community and not in a city
b.why: Self-determination is about who makes the decisions. Here the government listened but kept the final decision, so the community had no real say. Consulting people is a step, but it is not the same as them deciding.
b.clue: Being heard is different from being the decision maker.

draft.title: Self-determination
card: Self-determination is the right of a people to decide for themselves how they live and how they run their communities and lands.
For Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, it means holding the power to make decisions about their own lives, lands and communities.
Being asked for views is not enough if someone else makes the final decision. Having Indigenous people carry out a program is also not enough if others decided what it would be.
It can take many forms, such as Indigenous-run organisations that choose their own priorities and deliver services like health care or legal help.
draft.remember: Self-determination is about who holds the decision-making power, not who is consulted or who does the work.

a.q: Which of these is the clearest example of self-determination?
opts: An Aboriginal-run legal service chooses its own priorities
A department asks an Aboriginal group for its views first
A government hires Aboriginal staff to run its own program
A council informs elders of a plan it has already approved
a.why: Self-determination means Indigenous people hold the power to decide, and an organisation setting its own priorities does this. Asking for views is the most tempting wrong option, but the department still makes the decision.
a.clue: Look for who holds the final decision.

b.q: A state government wants to cut youth crime in a remote Aboriginal community. It holds a meeting, listens to views, then writes and runs the program itself. Why does this fall short of self-determination?
opts: The government kept the power to make the final decisions
The government aimed the program at young people only
The government paid for the program from its own budget
The government did not ask the community for its views
b.why: Self-determination depends on who decides. The government listened but still made the final decisions, so the community did not hold the power. The last option is wrong because the government did hold a meeting and listen.
b.clue: Listening to people is different from letting them decide.

a.best: An Aboriginal-run legal service chooses its own priorities

b.best: The government kept the power to make the final decisions

problems.detail: Why (b) says 'The last option is wrong because the government did hold a meeting and listen', but options are shown in random order, and the option it means ('did not ask the community for its views') is not last. A student could be confused or think the explanation contradicts the options. Name the option by its content instead of its position.

check.summary: The card and both questions are sound, and each has one clear right answer. Why (b) refers to 'the last option' by position, which will not match the shuffled order students see, so it should name the option by its content.
